title: Fairness, Conduct and Consumer Outcomes
summary: The board's responsibility for fair outcomes where AI makes or influences decisions: how bias arises, how fairness is tested, and how the board gains assurance on customer treatment.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The board's responsibility for fair outcomes where AI makes or influences decisions: how bias arises, how fairness is tested, and how the board gains assurance on customer treatment.
Learning Objectives: Explain how bias and proxy discrimination enter AI-driven decisions
Evaluate whether bias testing and outcome monitoring give real assurance
Identify the conduct, legal and reputational exposure of unfair outcomes
Syllabus: Sources of bias: historical data, proxies and feedback loops
Fairness measures in credit, insurance pricing and targeting
Consumer protection, fair treatment and non-discrimination obligations applied to AI
Case studies of AI bias harms and remediation
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for AI, risk and compliance
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
